Not very helpful or insightful- but I appreciate your enthusiasm and engagement.
Perhaps you need (among other things) more context...
I am writing a utility that will import maps from one RMMZ project to another.
Part of this process is identifying any accompanying resource files.
I'm sure I don't need to tell you- Maps contain events.
In the JSON data of a standard RMMZ map, you will observe that these events have (1) their pages with command lists, and (2) their move routes which also have their own command lists.
Additionally common events can be called from either of these command lists, and each common event (upon examination of  is its own commands list.
One of the commands that can be summoned by a map event and/or common event is `Show Animation`.
In RMMZ, `Show Animation` has a parameter that corresponds to an *.efkefc file.
Beyond just the resource files in the standard RMMZ data JSONs, there happen to be resource files (*.pngs and *.efkmodel) used by *.efkefc files as well (located in the `effects/textures/` and `effects/models/` folders).
So, in order to fully import a map from one RMMZ project to another, these files need to be taken into consideration.
Unfortunately, `animations in the help file` doesn't cover any of this.
Hence, I am asking here (in the JavaScript section of a forum that purports to offer support for RPG Maker MZ) if anybody (not including
@Andar
, who has admitted that he hasn`t worked with Effekseer himself and wanted me and everybody reading this thread to know that, despite trying to answer my query) has any experience with parsing *.efkefc files (using actual JavaScript and not `[loading] them with the program that created them) and might be able to help?
Have a great day and thanks in advance!

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
while that gives more context, it doesn't change the fact that effekseer and the effekseer community are still your best place to start - users there will probably have more knowledge on how those files work than users of MZ.
Because analysing binary files for data is almost impossible without having at least some basic concepts of how the binary file is constructed.

posts.author: Zeriab
posts.body:
Trying to figure out how the package structurally works can be a fun puzzle. That said, I suggest following the code for a more efficient way for figuring out the structure of the files.
A quick look in the MZ js files shows the following call being used to load effekseer animations:
Graphics.effekseer.loadEffect(url, 1, onLoad, onError);
Effekseer is open source and available. This looks like a promizing method to read:
https://github.com/effekseer/EffekseerForWebGL/blob/master/src/js/effekseer.src.js#L213
P.s: Multiple MZ CoreScript versions exists. I suggest looking up which Effekseer versions are used, and then checking the code for those versions to see what sort of difference there can be between them.
